description:
src/clients/ureq.rs:125: `let mut bytes = Vec::with_capacity(limit.min(8192));`. If limit = 10 MiB (default), this allocates 8 KiB up front, then grows via standard Vec doubling. Final body of 1 MiB CRL needs ~5 reallocations (8K → 16K → 32K → ... → 1 MiB), each copying the prefix.

Expected impact at scale: a path-validation workload fetching CRLs in the 100-KiB-to-2-MiB range pays ~6-10 unnecessary reallocations per fetch. For one-off validation this is irrelevant; for a batch validator running millions of chains, it adds up to seconds of avoidable memcpy.

reqwest::Response::content_length() would give a length hint when the responder sets Content-Length. ureq has the same: `response.headers().get(CONTENT_LENGTH)`. Use it as the with_capacity hint when present, fall back to limit.min(8192) when absent.

Minor — flagged because it's a quick win with no API change. Probably not worth a separate PR but worth a comment in the with_capacity line so future contributors don't 'optimise' it into something worse.
title: ReqwestFetcher streams body chunk-by-chunk; sync UreqFetcher allocates with Vec::with_capacity(limit.min(8192))
